sprint_log.response:
**Diana** 👋

Hey Sam — fair callout, totally on me. Here's where I'm redirecting focus:

• **Login screen is now #1** — wireframes by EOD today, full fidelity by tomorrow noon
• **Canvas background** — scrapping dark, moving to **white base + subtle gray grid** (standard infra diagramming convention, should've caught this earlier)
• **Empty state** — designing alongside canvas so new users have clear onboarding context when they first land
• Will drop everything in the **#infraviz-design** Figma file and ping for review before moving forward

No more assumptions on visual direction — I'll flag decisions like background color before implementing. Thanks for keeping me honest. 🙏

— Diana

Appreciate the quick feedback — keeps things moving! 🚀

— Diana

stories.title: Login Screen
stories.description: As a first-time user, I want a clean login page so my first impression of InfraViz is professional.

stories.title: White Canvas + Grid
stories.description: As a user, I want a white canvas with gray gridlines so the workspace feels familiar like Figma.

stories.title: Onboarding Tooltip
stories.description: As a new user, I want a tooltip on my first empty canvas so I know how to get started.
acceptance: Tooltip appears only on first visit
'Drag an AWS resource to start' copy

stories.title: Design Tokens
stories.description: As a developer, I want consistent design tokens so the UI feels cohesive across all components.

stories.title: Login Screen Design
stories.description: As a new user, I want a clear and accessible login screen so that I can securely access the InfraViz platform.
acceptance: Login form includes email and password fields
Error states are visually distinct and descriptive
Design meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standards
Figma frame delivered and linked in Jira

stories.title: Canvas Background Update
stories.description: As a user, I want a white canvas with a gray grid background so that infrastructure components are easy to distinguish and position.
acceptance: Gray grid overlay is subtle and non-distracting
Grid spacing follows 8pt design system baseline

stories.title: Empty State Design
stories.description: As a first-time user, I want an informative empty state on the canvas so that I understand how to start building my infrastructure diagram.
acceptance: Empty state includes illustrative icon and helper text
A clear call-to-action button is visible
State disappears once a component is added to canvas

stories.title: Component Drag Interaction
stories.description: As a user, I want to drag infrastructure components onto the canvas so that I can visually build and arrange my system architecture.
acceptance: Components snap to grid on drop
Drag preview shadow is visible during interaction
